name: Dry-Brined Roast Turkey with Classic Gravy

instructions.primary_message: This recipe can take 2 days (with a fresh turkey) or up to 5 days (with a frozen turkey). Plan accordingly and make sure you have enough space in your fridge.
FOR THE TURKEY (DRY-BRINING): If using a frozen turkey, thaw in the fridge for 2-3 days. If using a fresh turkey, skip this step.
instructions.secondary_message: 5.44 kg whole turkey, fresh or frozen

instructions.primary_message: Place a large (wire) cooling rack on top of a large roasting pan (the cooling rack should sit flush against the edges of the roasting pan). Set aside.
Place salt and sugar in a small bowl. Stir to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅓ cup kosher salt
2 tbsp brown sugar

instructions.primary_message: Remove neck and giblets from inside the turkey (if there are any) and discard.
Thoroughly pat turkey dry with paper towels, paying special attention to the inside cavity.
Rub sugar-salt mixture all over the outside and inside of the turkey, then carefully place it, breast side-up, on top of the cooling rack.
Place turkey in the fridge, uncovered (or very loosely tented with foil or parchment paper), for a minimum of 12 hours and up to 48 hours.
FOR THE TURKEY (BAKING): About 4 hours before you plan to serve the turkey, set it on the counter and allow to come to room temperature for 1 hour.
Once the turkey has come to room temperature, preheat oven to 325°F. Arrange oven rack in the lower position.
Carefully lift the wire rack and turkey out the roasting pan. Wipe away any excess salt or brine that has accumulated in the pan. Return wire rack and turkey to the roasting pan and set aside.
Small dice butter and place in a small bowl to soften.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 small pkg fresh rosemary
1 small pkg fresh thyme
1 lemon

instructions.primary_message: Remove half of the herbs from stems and mince the leaves; add to the bowl with the butter. (Reserve remaining herbs, still on their stems, for later use.)
Zest lemon into the bowl; use the back of a spoon to mash and combine the herb butter. (Reserve lemon for the next step.)
Quarter lemon and onion (with the peel). Halve garlic head crosswise. Stuff lemon, onion, and garlic inside the turkey along with the reserved herb sprigs.
Spread the herb butter over the turkey breast and legs.
Once the turkey is prepped, pour cold water through the wire rack into the roasting pan.
Place turkey in the oven and roast until the skin starts to turn golden, about 1 ½ hours.
Once the skin is golden, loosely cover the turkey with a piece of aluminum foil and continue to roast until the middle of a thigh or breast reaches 165°F, 1 hour more.
When the turkey is done, remove from the oven and transfer to a platter. Set aside to rest, still covered with foil, for 30 minutes.
FOR THE GRAVY: While the turkey is resting, carefully pour the drippings from the roasting pan into a medium bowl. Set aside to cool slightly, about 5 minutes.
Once the drippings have cooled, use a spoon or ladle to skim off and discard any fat that has settled on top.
Transfer 1 cup of the de-fatted drippings to a medium saucepan. Add flour and whisk to combine a smooth, thin paste.
Set the pan over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat.

Add broth, Worcestershire, and spices to the pan, then whisk to combine. Return to medium-high heat and bring to a simmer. Once simmering, reduce heat and continue to cook, stirring often, until gravy is thickened and flavors blend, about 8 minutes. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
710 ml chicken or vegetable broth
1 tsp Worcestershire sauce
½ tsp thyme, dried
kosher salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: If the gravy is too thin, combine water and cornstarch in a small bowl. Add to the pan, 1 tablespoon at a time, whisking well after each addition, until the gravy reaches desired thickness.
Carve turkey and serve with gravy on the side. Enjoy!
